{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg44jZdRTGxtPfxBLGKKR","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I rewrote `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program and updated `CMakeLists.txt`. The executable is still named `cholesky`, and I created no new files. It builds, and validation passes at every size and rank count I tried.\n\n**Design**\n- **Decomposition:** this is a blocked, right-looking Cholesky on 64-wide column panels. Panel `j` is owned by rank `j % P` and stays on that rank's GPU, with one GPU per rank.\n- **Padding:** the matrix is padded to a multiple of 64 with an identity block, which leaves the factor unchanged.\n- **CUDA kernels:** I wrote them by hand, so there is no cuBLAS dependency.\n  - A register-tiled FP64 matrix-multiply kernel does the trailing updates.\n  - A shared-memory kernel factors the diagonal block.\n  - A triangular-solve kernel does the panel solve.\n- **MPI:** the panels are broadcast through pinned host buffers. The owner of the next panel updates, factors and sends it first. The other ranks keep updating their trailing panels on the GPU during the broadcast.\n- **Input generation:** every rank builds its own panels of `B·Bᵀ + n·I` on its GPU. It uses the same `rand_r` sequence and seed as the original.\n- **OpenMP:** it parallelises the host-side gather and unpack of the result. It matters little because almost all the work is on the GPUs.\n- **Validation (`-v`):** `L·Lᵀ` is rebuilt and compared on the GPU of rank 0, using the original's tolerance.\n- **Failure and options:** a matrix that is not positive definite is reported on every rank, with the same error message as the original. `-n`, `-v`, `-r` and `-h` work as before, and only rank 0 prints.\n- **CMake:** it now requires MPI, OpenMP and the CUDA toolkit, and builds `cholesky.cpp` as CUDA. The default architectures are 70, 80, 86 and 90, and you can override them with `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`.\n\n**Results** on 4× RTX 3090 with n=16000, GFLOPS as the program reports it:\n\n| Ranks | Time | GFLOPS |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | 3806 ms | 359 |\n| 2 | 1921 ms | 711 |\n| 4 | 1291 ms | 1058 |\n\nAt n=1000 the 1-, 2- and 4-rank runs all gave a max relative error of about 8e-12. I also checked n=1 and n=70, which is not a multiple of 64.\n\n- **Timing scope:** the timed region covers only the factorisation, as in the original. The gather to rank 0 happens afterwards, and only with `-r` or `-v`.\n- **Gather memory:** that gather needs an `n×n` host buffer on rank 0.\n- **Rounding:** floating-point summation order differs from the sequential code, so results match to rounding error rather than bit for bit. That could change the `-r` hash if it is compared exactly.\n- **Not tested:** I did not try a multi-node run, a failing (not positive definite) input, or a build with a different `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":546,"cache_read_input_tokens":42605,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":546},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"faf763c4-249f-46d9-a8fc-3fd3bc46bae1","uuid":"5d5219a8-340a-49e5-9a9b-30919670efe1","timestamp":"2026-10-15T13:00:46.904Z","request_id":"req_011Cg44jXqGsxR3mZg5SDdbi"}
